privacy.title: Privacy notice
privacy.description: What Gusty collects, why, who helps us run it, and your rights.
privacy.intro: This notice explains, in plain language, what happens to your information when you use Gusty at heygusty.com.

sections.heading: Who we are
paragraphs: Gusty is run by Aniela Fidler-Wieruszewska, a sole trader based in the United Kingdom, trading as Gusty. She is responsible for your personal data (the "controller").
Questions about your data: hello@heygusty.com

sections.heading: What we collect
items: Your ideas and projects: what you write, and Gusty's readings, directions and next steps for them, plus the choices you make (for example, the mode you prefer).
Your email address, if you add one to keep your projects or to sign in.
Feedback you choose to send us.
A record of AI requests: which feature was used, when, and how much it cost to run. This record never includes what you wrote.
If you support Gusty: Stripe handles the payment. We can see your name, email address, the amount and the date in Stripe. We never see your card details.
Cookies: one to keep you signed in, and a short-lived one (one hour) when you bring guest projects into your account. We don't use advertising or tracking cookies, and we don't use analytics.

sections.heading: Why we use it
items: To run Gusty for you: saving your projects, preparing readings and next steps, and sending sign-in emails. This is needed to provide the service you asked for.
To keep Gusty safe and affordable: daily limits, preventing misuse and fixing problems. This is in our legitimate interests.
To improve Gusty from the feedback you choose to send. This is in our legitimate interests.
To handle support payments and keep financial records, as the law requires.

sections.heading: How Gusty uses AI
paragraphs: When Gusty reads your idea or suggests steps, the text of that project is sent to Anthropic, the company that makes the Claude AI, to prepare the answer. Under Anthropic's commercial terms, this text isn't used to train their models.

When you ask Gusty to search for opportunities, Claude searches the web for you. The search words describe your idea's theme and the area you gave (for example “community repair café, Hackney”), and go to the search engine Anthropic uses. They never include your name or email. What Gusty finds is saved with your project, only for you.

Looking for research that backs your idea works the same way: the search words describe your idea's theme, never you, and the sources Gusty finds are saved with your project, only for you. When you ask Gusty to describe how you write, only your own writing about that project is sent.

When you bring a funder's papers into an application space (a PDF, pasted text or a public link), they're sent to Anthropic for Claude to read, then discarded. Gusty keeps only what it read from them, such as the questions and rules, with your project. To see how your project fits, or to draft an answer, Gusty sends that project, its story, what it read from the funder's papers and anything you've written for that answer.

If you bring in a PDF, it's sent to Anthropic for Claude to read, then discarded: Gusty doesn't keep the file. It keeps only its notes (a short summary and what the document says you've done), which you can read and delete on the project page.

Your projects are private to you. We never show them to other people who use Gusty, and we never use one person's ideas to make suggestions for someone else: each request only includes the project you're working on.
AI suggestions can be wrong. Please avoid including sensitive details, such as health information, about yourself or other people in your ideas.

sections.heading: Who helps us run Gusty
paragraphs: These companies process data on our behalf, only to provide their service to us:
items: Supabase: database and sign-in (EU).
Render: hosting the website (Frankfurt, Germany).
Anthropic: AI readings, suggestions and web searches for opportunities (United States).
Resend: sending sign-in emails.
Stripe: support payments and receipts.
ImprovMX: forwarding emails sent to hello@heygusty.com.
after: Some of these providers are based in, or may process data in, the United States. Where they do, they rely on safeguards recognised under UK data protection law, such as the UK's data bridge or standard contractual clauses. We don't sell your data or share it for advertising.

sections.heading: How long we keep it
items: Your projects and email address: until you delete them or your account.
The record of AI requests: deleted with your account.
Feedback: kept while it's useful for improving Gusty. It's no longer linked to you once you delete your account.
Payment records: kept by Stripe, and by us for as long as UK tax law requires.

sections.heading: Your rights
paragraphs: You can ask to see, correct or delete your data, to receive a copy of it, or to object to or restrict how we use it. You can download your projects and delete your account yourself on My Projects. For anything else, email hello@heygusty.com and we'll reply within one month.
If you're unhappy with how we handle your data, you can complain to the Information Commissioner's Office (ico.org.uk). We'd appreciate the chance to put things right first.

sections.heading: Changes
paragraphs: If we change how we use your data, we'll update this page and the date at the top.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.description: The simple rules for using Gusty.
terms.intro: These terms are an agreement between you and Gusty. We've kept them short and plain. By using Gusty, you agree to them.

sections.heading: Who we are
paragraphs: Gusty is run by Aniela Fidler-Wieruszewska, a sole trader based in the United Kingdom, trading as Gusty. Contact: hello@heygusty.com

sections.heading: Gusty is new
paragraphs: Gusty is in early testing. Features may change, and things may sometimes go wrong or be unavailable. We'll always try to keep your work safe.

sections.heading: AI suggestions are suggestions
paragraphs: Gusty's readings, directions and steps are prepared by AI. They can be wrong or incomplete, so please check anything important yourself. Gusty doesn't give legal, financial or other professional advice, and can't promise funding or results.

sections.heading: Your work stays yours
paragraphs: What you write in Gusty belongs to you. You allow us to store and process it only to run Gusty for you, as described in our privacy notice. You can download or delete your projects at any time.

sections.heading: Your ideas stay private
paragraphs: We never share your ideas or projects with other people who use Gusty, and we never use one person's ideas to make suggestions for someone else. When Gusty helps with a project, it works only from that project.

Many people have similar ideas on their own, and Gusty may suggest similar directions or steps to different people because its suggestions come from general knowledge. We can't be responsible for other people having, developing or launching ideas similar to yours. Gusty doesn't give your ideas legal protection; if that matters to you, you may want to look into it before sharing your idea widely.

sections.heading: Using Gusty fairly
paragraphs: Please don't use Gusty to break the law, to harm or harass anyone, to try to get around its security or limits, or to overload it. We may pause or close accounts that do.

sections.heading: Supporting Gusty
paragraphs: Support payments are voluntary and are handled by Stripe. Gusty isn't a registered charity, so support isn't tax-deductible, and it doesn't unlock extra features. You can stop monthly support at any time. If you change your mind, email hello@heygusty.com within 14 days of a payment for a full refund.

sections.heading: Our responsibility to you
paragraphs: We're responsible for loss or damage you suffer that is a foreseeable result of us breaking these terms or not taking reasonable care. We're not responsible for loss that wasn't foreseeable, or for business losses. Nothing in these terms limits your rights under consumer law, or our responsibility where the law doesn't allow it to be limited.

sections.heading: Leaving Gusty
paragraphs: You can stop using Gusty and delete your account at any time on My Projects.

sections.heading: Law
paragraphs: These terms are governed by the law of the part of the United Kingdom where you live, and you can bring any claim in your local courts.

sections.heading: Changes
paragraphs: If we change these terms, we'll update this page and the date at the top.

bank.experienceIntro: What you've done before, what you've won, what people have said and numbers that matter. In your own words: funders love real examples.

kinds.win: Funding or an award I've had

bank.textLabel: Tell it in your own words
bank.textHint: For example: “Ran a summer bike club for 12 kids in 2024. Every one of them kept riding.”
bank.urlLabel: A link, if there is one (optional)
bank.emptyExperience: Nothing here yet. Even small things count: a stall you ran, a thank-you note, a number of people who came.

bank.researchIntro: Gusty looks for recent studies, official figures and trusted reports that show the need for your idea, or the good it does. Funders often ask for this.
bank.researchWhat: A research search reads real web pages, so each one costs Gusty a little to run (about 10p to 30p). That's why there's a small daily allowance, separate from deep searches.
bank.researchAllowanceProject: One research search per project each day.
bank.researchRunning: Gusty is looking for research. This can take a minute or two, and you can leave this page: anything it finds will be here.
bank.researchFailed: The last research search didn't finish. Nothing was used up: you can try again.
bank.researchLimitProject: You've already looked for research for this project today. You can look again tomorrow.
bank.researchLimitPerson: You've used today's {max} research searches. They reset within a day.
bank.researchNone: Nothing yet. Gusty only keeps sources it actually read, with a link to each.

researchErrors.limit: Gusty is resting for today. Please try again tomorrow.

applications.listIntro: One space for each thing you'd like to apply for. Bring in the funder's papers and Gusty will show you what they're looking for and how your project fits.
applications.pageIntro: Bring in the funder's papers. Gusty reads them, keeps what matters, and shows you how your project fits. Nothing is sent to the funder.
applications.addIntro: The application form or questions, guidance notes, terms and conditions, or a list of past winners. Add as many as you have.
applications.waysLabel: How would you like to bring it in?
applications.fileHint: Up to 10 MB and 100 pages. Gusty keeps what it reads, not the file.
applications.pasteHint: For example, copy the questions from the funder's online form. Gusty keeps what it reads, not the pasted text.
applications.linkHint: Gusty can open public pages only. If it needs a login (like a private Google Doc or a funder portal), download it as a PDF or paste the text instead.
applications.reading: Gusty is reading it. This can take up to a minute.
applications.added: Gusty has read it and kept what matters.

applications.briefTitle: What this funder is looking for
applications.briefIntro: Read from their papers and quoted as they put it. Always check the original before you apply: funders change their rules, and Gusty can misread.
applications.nothingYet: Bring in at least one of the funder's papers to see this.
applications.demoReadingNotice: Demo mode: this is a made-up example, not what your paper says. Gusty's real reading starts once the AI key is set up.
applications.fitIntro: Gusty's view, from your project, your story and the funder's papers. It's a suggestion, not a decision: only the funder decides who gets funding.
applications.fitRunning: Gusty is working out how your project fits. This takes about a minute.
applications.fitFailed: Gusty couldn't work this out just now.
applications.fitAgainHint: Added to your story since? Gusty can look again.
applications.wordsIntro: The funder's key phrases, and how you might say the same thing in your own voice.
applications.demoFitNotice: Demo mode: this is a made-up example. Gusty's real view appears once the AI key is set up.

weak.body: There's little overlap so far, or a rule to check. It may be worth asking them, or looking elsewhere.

applications.soundLikeMeHint: Off: Gusty mirrors the funder's language, which funders tend to respond to. On: your own voice comes first. Applies the next time Gusty drafts.

account.title: Your account
account.guest: You're using Gusty as a guest. Add your email so your projects are kept safe and you can sign in on any device.
account.signedOut: You're not signed in. Sign in with your email to see your account.
account.downloadHint: A plain document with everything you've saved: your ideas, plans, notes, story and applications.
account.downloadData: Or download it as a data file (for moving to another tool)
account.leaveBody: You can delete your account and everything in it at any time. This can't be undone, so you may want to download your projects first.
